title: Largest Element in an Array after Merge Operations
statement:
`nums` holds positive integers. As often as you like (including never), you may pick two neighbours `nums[i]` and `nums[i + 1]` where the left one is not larger than the right one (`nums[i] <= nums[i + 1]`), remove the left one, and replace the right one by their sum, so the array becomes one element shorter.

Return the biggest value that any element of the array can reach after some sequence of these merges.
notes:
## Intuition

Trying every order of merges (the brute force) explodes quickly. The key observation is that a merge only ever feeds a value into its **right** neighbour, and a bigger right value accepts more. So walk from the right end and keep one running block: the block can swallow the next element on its left whenever that element is not larger than the block. If it is larger, nothing on the right can ever reach past it, so that element starts a new block.

A new block only starts when its first element is already bigger than the old block, so the running value never decreases. The block alive at the end is therefore the largest one.

## Approach

1. Set `current` to the last element.
2. Move `i` from the second-to-last index down to `0`.
3. If `nums[i] <= current`, merge: add `nums[i]` to `current`.
4. Otherwise `nums[i]` cannot be merged, so it becomes the new `current`.
5. Return `current`.

## Example 1, step by step

`nums = [2, 3, 7, 9, 3]`. Start with `current = 3`. At `i = 3`, `9 > 3`, so `current = 9`. At `i = 2`, `7 <= 9`, so `current = 16`. At `i = 1`, `3 <= 16`, so `current = 19`. At `i = 0`, `2 <= 19`, so `current = 21`. The answer is `21`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n): one pass from right to left.
- Space: O(1): only the running block is stored.

## Pitfalls

- Scanning left to right fails: `[5, 3, 3]` gives `11` only because the two 3s merge first, which a left-to-right pass would miss.
- The sum can reach about 10^11, so Java and C need a 64-bit type (`long` / `long long`).
- The comparison is `<=`: equal neighbours may merge.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `current` | value of the block being built from the right |
| `i` | index of the element we try to merge into the block |

narration.2: Begin the running block with the last element, since merges always flow to the right.
narration.4: Walk leftwards from the second-to-last element.
narration.5: Can this element merge into the block on its right? Only if it is not larger.
narration.6: Yes: the block absorbs it and grows.
narration.8: No: this element is larger than the whole block, so it starts a new, bigger block.
narration.11: The block never shrinks, so the final block is the largest value reachable.
